messages:
maria: Heads-up — I've been tracking a recurring surge in missing spans in prod aggregation for the last ~48h. Pattern seems to spike roughly every ~6 hours. Starting a quick triage thread. cc @chris @ashwin
chris: Thanks. Can you paste the query you used to detect the gap?
maria: Sure, quick check I ran:```
SELECT count(*) as span_count, floor(extract(epoch from timestamp)/3600) as hour 
FROM spans
WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '48 hours'
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour DESC
```
chris: Nice. I can see the dips. ashwin any ETL jobs that line up with those windows?
ashwin: Looking at job-runner, we had a batch overlap and spikes in processing time at ~03:05-03:20 UTC yesterday and today. Pulling worker logs now.
erin: We should avoid config changes to aggregator during triage. Let's assign clear owners and timelines so we don't have duplicate work.
maria: Proposal: ashwin -> investigate ETL timings + infra (OOMs etc) (48h RCA). chris -> check aggregator rollouts & runbook + do config canary (24h). erin -> add detection/alert and dashboards (today). I'll own postmortem updates and tracking (72h). Thoughts?
chris: Sounds good. I'll also check deploy history for any recent default changes to group_by or rollup thresholds.
ashwin: quick note: job-runner logs show container OOM restarts at ~03:10 UTC, repeated. Suspect memory pressure triggering partial processing and lost spans. Pasting log snippet:```
[2026-02-12T03:10:11Z] kubelet: OOMKilled container=etl-worker-7c9f
[2026-02-12T03:10:12Z] etl-worker: restarting batch id=8742
```
erin: I'll open an alert: span-drop-rate >= 0.5% over 10m -> ping #oncall + playbook. Can someone verify thresholds?
observability-bot: Created alert "span-drop-rate" (severity: p2). Runbook attached: /playbooks/span-drop.md. Notifying #oncall.
maria: Chris — any config rollouts around Nov/Dec that could change aggregation semantics?
chris: Found a rollout on 2024-11-07 for aggregator v2 that changed default group_by behavior (PR #4523). Rolling a canary to revert just the default parameter to previous behavior for safety. Will post canary link.
nashwin: If OOM is the root cause, mitigation plan: increase ETL worker memory to 4Gi, add pod anti-affinity for heavy shards during batch windows, and capture heap dumps during next window. I'll try a heap dump capture next cycle.
erin: PR for alert + dashboard ready: https://git.internal/repo/alerts/pull/120 — requesting review.
maria: Quick action-item recap (I'll track these in the incident tracker):
1) ashwin — investigate OOM restarts, attach heap dumps + propose infra change (due +48h).
2) chris — canary revert of aggregation default + add runbook entry and rollback play (due +24h).
3) erin — alert + dashboards (PR opened).
4) maria — update postmortem skeleton with timeline and service-level impact, link to SLA metrics (due +72h).
Please react with :white_check_mark: when you've started/finished.
chris: :white_check_mark: started rollback canary, will update with rollout link and results.
ashwin: Started capturing heap dump now, pushing logs to the incident bucket: https://storage.internal/incidents/2046002468/logs
erin: Alert PR merged and dashboard published — will add runbook steps into /playbooks soon.
maria: Thanks all. Let's also add a short-term scheduled check for the next 2 weeks to catch recurrence and validate the fix. I'll add a recurring 15m check-in invite for the owners.
chris: I'll run a small synthetic load after canary to confirm group_by behavior and span counts.
nashwin: If the heap dump confirms memory leak, I'll propose a minor code patch and schedule a hotfix.
erin: I'll monitor the new alert and adjust thresholds if we get noisy signals.
maria: Ok — tracking notes updated in incident tracker and will attach this thread to the postmortem. Closing triage for now, please update the tracker with status changes.
